checklist_item: Is Dayton Foundation Plus a DAF sponsor; is this DAF-to-DAF; extend whitelist?
claim_as_stated: Whether such lines are DAF-to-DAF is queued (P-B5102-01); Dayton Foundation Plus described as a DAF holder outside the DAFRC panel.
source_date: Dayton Plus FYE 2022-06-30 and 2023-06-30; BMF cached 2026-11-14
exact_values_found: Dayton Plus 990 FYE 2022-06-30: Part IV line 6 = 1; Schedule A 509(a)(3) Type II, one supported organisation THE DAYTON FOUNDATION (EIN 316027287), which is its sole member; Schedule D Part I column (a) DAFs blank, column (b) funds and other accounts: 78 held, contributions $389,738,765, grants $17,671,980, EOY $399,708,444 (total assets $412.1m, up from $83.5m). FYE 2023: column (b) 68 / $408.7m, column (a) blank. non-dafrc-daf-filers-990.csv: column (a) blank FY2020-24. BMF: subsection 03, foundation 17, NTEE T11, ruling 200304. Not in the DAFRC panel; The Dayton Foundation is whitelisted (W3).
discrepancies: Dayton Plus is not a DAF sponsor on its own filings (no Schedule D column (a) DAFs in any year), so the study's phrase other DAF holders is loose.
contradictory_evidence: Marin's DAF grants spike in the same year, so the money likely left a DAF.
interpretation_challenge: Not DAF-to-DAF under the repo's definition. The whitelist exists to stop DAF grants being double counted in DAFRC market totals; Dayton Plus is not in the panel and reports no DAFs, so there is no double count to remove. Do not extend the whitelist on this case; treat it as a sponsor-family fund transfer, named in the study and covered by the existing non-DAFRC sensitivity.
